newsitem.title: NEPAL: Nepali transport operators raise fares 20 pct.
newsitem.headline: Nepali transport operators raise fares 20 pct.

text.p: Private Nepali transport operators have raised the fares of all public transport vehicles by 20 percent following a recent increase in oil prices in the Himalayan kingdom, union officials said on Tuesday.
"The increased rates will be operative in Kathmandu from Tuesday," Hom Prasad Adhikary, general secretary of the Federation of the Nepalese Transport Entrepreneurs Association (FNTEA), told Reuters.
He said the new rates came into effect for rest of the kingdom on Monday.
Last month Nepal raised fuel prices by 14.7 percent for petrol, 15.7 percent for kerosene and 27 percent for diesel.

But last week the government, making a partial retreat in the face of strong protests led by communists in the ruling coalition, rolled back the prices of diesel and kerosene by 11.4 and 4.5 percent respectively.
Union officials said FNTEA had demanded that the government reduce the fuel prices to their previous levels by the end of July or face an additional 15 percent increase in the public transport fares.
FNTEA members own public transport vehicles including buses, taxis and trucks. Government officials said a meeting with transport operators was scheduled for Tuesday.
